prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer faces downward toward a counter or table surface roughly 0.7 to 1.0 m below the head, with no other people in the scene and the wearer's own torso and arms closest at 0.2 to 0.5 m in the lower foreground. In frames 1 and 5, the camera looks down and slightly left at a small metal bowl, a round lid, and a large appliance base spaced 0.1 to 0.3 m apart on the surface within arm's reach, whereas in frames 2 through 4 the viewpoint shifts right to center directly above a wet grinder drum at about 0.4 to 0.6 m depth while the right hand holds a spatula 0.3 to 0.4 m away above and inside the drum. The wearer's right arm and hand enter from the right edge to partially occlude the grinder drum and its internal rollers in frames 2 to 4, while the lower body remains partially out of view at the bottom edge across all frames and the left hand reaches toward the small bowl at the lower left in frames 1 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the elevated height of the wearer's torso, right forearm, and grinder rim from the lower counter surface and recessed interior of the drum. However, the depth map is unreliable in frames 1 and 5 where motion blur flattens the bowls and counter into indistinct dark regions, and in frames 2 to 4 where dark floor tiles and shadowed areas to the right of the counter drop to pitch black as if infinitely far away.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to parse the downward-facing egocentric scene containing the camera wearer's lower body at 0.2 to 0.4 m in the bottom foreground and kitchen objects 0.4 to 0.8 m below on the counter within arm's reach, with no other people present or looking toward the camera. Across the sequence, as the camera turns right from the counter in frame 1 to center over the grinder drum in frames 2 to 4 and turns back left in frame 5, the masks track the right arm reaching in from the right edge (0.3 to 0.5 m away) over the drum and the left hand reaching forward at the bottom-left (0.5 to 0.7 m away) in frame 5. In frame 2, the map cleanly isolates the white spatula ('spoon') held in the right hand from the white batter immediately below it, and in frame 3 it separates the overlapping right arm ('person') from the circular grinder drum ('bowl') underneath, boundaries that are low-contrast in the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable: it hallucinates a fragmented 'person' mask over the counter and blurred container in frame 1, misclassifies the wearer's patterned clothing at the bottom as a 'sandwich' in frames 2, 4, and 5, labels the grinder interior and counter as a 'dining table' in frame 4, and misses the plastic lid, mixer housing, and internal grinder stones entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 5, and detects only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in frames 3 and 4 at roughly 0.3 to 0.4 m in front of and below the camera, with no body skeletons or other people present in the scene. In frames 3 and 4, the detected right hand is positioned near the center-right just above the grinder drum well within arm's reach, oriented with the wrist toward the right and fingers curled downward and left around the spatula handle as the hand shifts slightly upward and right between the two frames. Because the camera wearer faces downward toward the counter, their head and upper torso are out of view behind the camera while their lower torso and left arm in frames 1 and 5 remain unrendered. This map makes the exact 3D finger flexion and wrist orientation of the grasping right hand explicit in frames 3 and 4 where skin tones and motion blur obscure the knuckles in the RGB strip. However, it is unreliable across the rest of the sequence, completely failing to detect the visible right hand in frame 2, the reaching left arm and hand at the lower left of frames 1 and 5, and the visible lower body across all five frames.
